_note: THE STORAGE COMPATIBILITY DECLARATION for the diner checkout record (D08 B1, R2).
Reviewed source, not a generated file. release/lib/storage.mjs is the rule that reads it;
release/README.md explains it for a human.
WHAT IT STATES. The exact (version, semantics) pairs this build WRITES and can READ under
the key below. The release gate refuses to promote a build unless it can read every pair
the served build writes or reads — as SET CONTAINMENT over these declared pairs, never
as a numeric comparison, on every promotion path (deploy, redeploy, rollback, bootstrap).
version 1 names the UNVERSIONED D04/D (#663) shape, which carries no v field and is
upgraded by CheckoutCoordinatorService.upgradeV1(). version 2 is CHECKOUT_RECORD_VERSION.
semantics names what a record of that version MEANS to a reader; bump it (and list the
new pair in reads/writes) when a change would make an OLDER reader mishandle an
outstanding issued command even though the version number did not move.
THE TRIPWIRE. reviewedSources are the sha256 of the files that implement the reader, the
writer, and the storage layer that serializes the record (StorageService,
SessionStorageService, StorageModule). release/cli.mjs stamp refuses a candidate whose
files no longer match, and
release/tests/storage.test.mjs fails the pull request first — so a change to the
checkout record code cannot reach certification without somebody re-affirming this
declaration (recompute with: node release/cli.mjs storage-reviewed --write).
THE BEHAVIOURAL PROOF is src/app/_services/checkout-record-storage.contract.spec.ts,
which drives the real coordinator with a record of every declared read pair and
asserts it is recovered under the SAME key with its issued command intact.
WHERE THE BYTES ARE (Codex P2 on #687). key is the logical key the coordinator uses;
physicalKey is where the bytes actually sit in sessionStorage — SessionStorageService
prepends the ROOT prefix (AppModule's StorageModule.forRoot) as [prefix]key. encoding
names the string StorageService stores: json-value-envelope is JSON.stringify({value:
record}). A served build's records are found only where and as it left them, so the
gate refuses a candidate whose store, key, physicalKey or encoding differs from the
served build's, and the contract spec seeds RAW bytes at physicalKey through the real
AppModule configuration rather than through the writer it is testing.
